description: At any font scale, the Classic, Minimal and Creative Word exports draw the same line pitch as the Preview, as Professional and Modern have done since #88. A parity profile at a fractional size proves it and guards it.

userStories.title: Classic, Minimal and Creative Word line pitch follows the Preview at fractional sizes
userStories.description: As a user who scales their CV's font, I want the Word file's line spacing to match the Preview for Classic, Minimal and Creative, so that pages break and read the same everywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Every call. In the three generators, every `exactLineSpacing` call receives the unrounded size of the element it spaces. Run `w:sz` values are unchanged.
Default exports. At scale 1 with default sizes, the Classic, Minimal and Creative DOCX for the e2e fixture are byte-identical to before (hash of `word/document.xml` recorded before and after).
Professional and Modern. Their DOCX are byte-identical to before for the same inputs (hashes recorded).
Unit test. `D/docx-line-spacing.test.ts` asserts the pitch against the Preview px for all five templates, at scales 0.8, 1 and 1.2. It fails on the pre-story generators and passes after.

Word re-measure. For each of the three templates at `per-property-control` sizes, Word's rendered body line pitch is within ±1.5 px of the Preview's, per baseline. Measured with the `docx-word-parity.md` method; the measurements are recorded in `progress.txt` and the doc.
FR-1: No change to `e2e/parity` comparison logic, tolerances or the KNOWN list, beyond the new profile and its id.
FR-2: Only the three generator files, `docx-line-spacing.test.ts` and the docs change under `src/` and `docs/` for US-001.
FR-3: The default-size output stays byte-identical. That is how the change stays safe for existing users.
Regression constraint: `pnpm test:parity`: every existing row keeps its verdict, and only the new rows are added.
Regression constraint: `pnpm test:visual` is unchanged (Preview).
Regression constraint: The e2e DOCX layout specs and the geometry and letter-spacing tests pass unmodified.
Verification: The `CLAUDE.md` §14 baseline, plus `pnpm test:parity` (report sha recorded; row diff against the previous report: only the new rows) and `pnpm test:visual`.

Verification: Export validation: DOCX hashes for the unchanged cases (default sizes for all five templates; Professional and Modern at fractional sizes); a Word COM measurement for the three templates at fractional sizes.
Verification: `code-reviewer`. `ui-expert` is NOT_APPLICABLE (no UI).
FAIL condition: Any default-size DOCX or any Professional/Modern DOCX changes.
FAIL condition: A `fractional-size` row is NEW after the fix, or an existing row changes verdict.
FAIL condition: A tolerance is changed or a KNOWN entry is added to pass.
BLOCKER condition: The Word COM measurement cannot run on the machine (Word missing). Report it; the owner decides whether XML-level evidence is enough.
BLOCKER condition: A title or heading row at the new profile turns NEW after the fix, showing another rounding path. Report it; widen the scope only by PRD update.
Out of scope: A horizontal width scale (`w:w`) or tracking from unrounded sizes for these three templates. That would be a separate fidelity change.
Out of scope: Baseline raise (`w:position`) for Georgia headings.
Out of scope: Spacer lines, page layout, and any Preview change.
Out of scope: The KNOWN `US-016-html-body-line-height` entry.

userStories.title: A parity profile guards line height at fractional sizes

acceptanceCriteria: The profile. A `fractional-size` profile exists, with `per-property-control`'s layout and `rowGroups: ['body-line-height']`, covering all five templates. It is added to the `ProfileId` union.
MATCH. Its five `line-height:bodyText` rows are MATCH. NEW stays 0, and KNOWN stays 3, unchanged.
It catches the defect. With US-001's generator change reverted locally, the classic, minimal and creative rows of this profile are NEW. Run as evidence and not committed; the output is recorded.
